meta.description: Improvement over the baseline in each quarter of the validation year. Its standard deviation is the noise level the holdout has to clear.

sources.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Economic Data
sources.licence: FRED API Terms of Use (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html). The terms require the notice "This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis", which the site prints. Series owned by third parties carry the word "Copyright" in their notes and need the owner's permission beyond personal use, so the catalogue holds only series published by US federal agencies (public domain) and the collector stops on any series whose notes say Copyright. The terms do not address storing data.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; most series are monthly
sources.typical_lag: two to eight weeks after the month ends, depending on the series

sources.name: BIS statistics (policy rates, consumer prices, exchange rates, effective exchange rates)
sources.licence: Terms of permitted use of BIS statistics (https://www.bis.org/terms_statistics.htm). Use is unrestricted provided the BIS is cited as the source, the use does not imply endorsement, and inclusion in a commercial product brings no additional charge to users. The statistics are not investment advice. The site cites the BIS under every table.

sources.name: OpenDOSM (Department of Statistics Malaysia)
sources.licence: DOSM Open Data License as shown in the OpenDOSM FAQ. It permits copying, publishing, adapting and commercial use; the datasets must not be used in a way that suggests official status or endorsement. The text was read on an archived copy of the FAQ (opendosm.netlify.app), not on open.dosm.gov.my itself, so re-read it there.

sources.name: Indeed Job Postings Index
sources.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, stated in the repository README: free for public use as long as Indeed Hiring Lab is cited as a source.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; daily index refreshed weekly

limitations: The target is each series' monthly move one month ahead. Errors are divided by the series' own mean absolute month-to-month change in the training period.
Models are fitted once on data before the validation year and are not refitted on later months when forecasting them.
Scored on latest published values, not on the values first published, so the test is kinder than real time. First-published values are being stored from the first run on.

finding.label: explanation
finding.reason: No model beat the naive baseline on the holdout months by more than the fold-to-fold spread, so nothing on these pages is a forecast. No signal found.

verdict.statement: No signal found: the naive baseline is published.
